reason: The text presents God's direct instruction to David: 'You shall shepherd my people Israel' (תִרְעֶה אֶת־עַמִּי יִשְׂרָאֵל). The Hebrew root רעה (ra'ah/shepherd) fundamentally emphasizes care and stewardship of the flock. Additionally, the passage demonstrates this principle through David's refusal to drink water that his soldiers obtained at great risk, saying 'Shall I drink the blood of these men who risked their lives?' This shows leadership as requiring respect for and protection of the people's welfare. The elders recognize David's fitness to lead precisely because he had previously been the one who 'led out and brought in Israel' - military leadership exercised on behalf of the people, not personal glory. These elements together establish shepherding/caring for the people's welfare as the divine model for David's kingship.
